    Count k-mers in sequences

    Source: R/bio-sequence.R
    bio_kmer_count.Rd

    Counts overlapping k-mers (substrings of length k) in each sequence and returns them as one column per k-mer, ready for modelling. For DNA and RNA with k up to 6 every possible k-mer gets a column; otherwise the k-mers observed in the data are used.

    Usage

    bio_kmer_count(
  .data,
  seq = NULL,
  k = 3,
  normalise = FALSE,
  vocabulary = NULL,
  prefix = "kmer_"
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame, tibble or bio_seq_tbl().

    seq

    <tidy-select> The sequence column. Can be omitted for a <bio_seq_tbl>.

    k

    K-mer length.

    normalise

    If TRUE, return frequencies (counts divided by the number of k-mers in the sequence) instead of counts.

    vocabulary

    Optional character vector of k-mers to count.

    prefix

    Prefix for the new column names.

    Value

    .data with one numeric column per k-mer, named paste0(prefix, kmer).

    Examples

    tibble::tibble(id = 1:2, seq = c("ACGTACGT", "GGGCCCAA")) |>
  bio_kmer_count(seq, k = 2)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 18
#>      id seq      kmer_AA kmer_AC kmer_AG kmer_AT kmer_CA kmer_CC kmer_CG kmer_CT
#>   <int> <chr>      <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1     1 ACGTACGT       0       2       0       0       0       0       2       0
#> 2     2 GGGCCCAA       1       0       0       0       1       2       0       0
#> # ℹ 8 more variables: kmer_GA <dbl>, kmer_GC <dbl>, kmer_GG <dbl>,
#> #   kmer_GT <dbl>, kmer_TA <dbl>, kmer_TC <dbl>, kmer_TG <dbl>, kmer_TT <dbl>
